prompts.template: Assess [my recording or transcript] for [target listener]. Identify two issues that affect understanding and give corrections and a retry exercise. Cite what is audible if you have audio; with text only, focus on organization and wording.

prompts.title: Localize software interface strings
prompts.description: Preserve variables, terminology, and length limits.
prompts.template: Localize [interface strings] for [target language and region] using [glossary, placement, and character limits]. Preserve keys, placeholders, escape sequences, and tags. Return translations and context questions by key, with shorter alternatives for strings that exceed limits.

prompts.title: Build a bilingual glossary
prompts.description: Specify preferred translations, variants, and scope.
prompts.template: Use [bilingual material] to build a glossary for [industry and audience]. Give original term, preferred translation, meaning, source example, and usage scope. Explain important conflicts and open questions and include three example uses.

prompts.title: Check a translation against the original
prompts.description: Find omissions, additions, and inconsistent terminology.
prompts.template: Compare [source text] and [translation] paragraph by paragraph for [language and use case]. Record omissions, mistranslations, number errors, and term inconsistencies. Give original, current version, revision, and severity. Separate style preferences from factual issues.

prompts.title: Compare how to say something in different registers
prompts.description: Choose wording that fits the relationship and setting.
prompts.template: Express [intended meaning] in [language and region] three ways for [different audiences or relationships]. Explain formality, naturalness, and possible misunderstandings. Give a natural response the other person might use.

prompts.title: Rewrite second-language text for natural phrasing
prompts.description: Keep the meaning, compare literal wording, and extract reusable patterns.
prompts.template: Rewrite this [target language] draft for [context and desired tone] so it sounds natural to a native speaker without changing my meaning: [draft text]. Give the revised version first, then show a table of 3 to 5 changes that improved naturalness most, and extract 3 reusable sentence patterns I can apply next time.

prompts.title: Adapt idioms and cultural references
prompts.description: Explain the literal gap and offer three options from close translation to transcreation.
prompts.template: Adapt [idiom, metaphor, or cultural reference] from [source language] for [target language and audience]. Explain its real meaning and tone in the source culture, note what a literal translation would lose or distort, and provide three options: close to the original, natural equivalent, and culturally adapted, with when to use each.

prompts.title: Turn a passage into a shadowing practice script
prompts.description: Mark thought groups, stressed words, linking, and tricky sounds.
prompts.template: Turn this [target language] passage into a shadowing script for a [learner level] learner: [practice text]. Mark natural thought-group pauses, key stressed words, common linking or reductions, and easily mispronounced sounds, then give a three-round drill from slow to natural speed.

prompts.title: Prepare a context brief for localization translators
prompts.description: Specify UI placement, character limits, variable meanings, and do-not-translate terms.
prompts.template: Based on [strings or copy to translate] and [product context and target market], write a translator context brief. For each item or group, note where it appears in the UI, character or layout limits, what each placeholder represents, do-not-translate terms, and any wording that could be misinterpreted.

prompts.title: Write a verifiable value proposition
prompts.description: Explain the difference and outcome with evidence.
prompts.template: Use [product facts and evidence] to write a value proposition for [audience and situation]. State what they do now, their obstacle, promised outcome, and evidence. Give two distinct positioning options and a test that could separate them.

prompts.title: Build a channel content calendar
prompts.description: Connect topics, production, and verification to a goal.
prompts.template: Plan content for [audience and communication goal] across [channels and dates]. For each item give task, audience question, source material, owner, deadline, and success measure. Prioritize ideas that can be produced with existing material.

prompts.title: Plan how to run a marketing campaign
prompts.description: Make channel actions, success measures, and evidence gaps explicit.
prompts.template: Plan a campaign for [product and goal] within [channels, time, and budget]. List tasks, materials, owners, and metrics for validation, launch, and review. Separate known audience evidence from assumptions and explain when to scale back or adjust.

prompts.title: Outline a landing page
prompts.description: Connect the promise, proof, and next action.
prompts.template: The goal is [desired action]. Plan a landing page for [product and audience]. Outline the hero, problem, outcome, usage, proof, questions, and call to action. For each section specify the question it answers and the material needed. Mark unsupported claims.

prompts.title: Write a search-informed content brief
prompts.description: Use real questions and a verifiable outline.
prompts.template: Create a content brief for [topic and readers] using [queries or search results] to infer intent. Give the main and related questions, structure, original material, and sources. Do not estimate search volume or competition without evidence.

prompts.title: Write ad variants you can test
prompts.description: Isolate one selling angle or variable per version.
prompts.template: Write ad variants for [product and audience] in [channel and length]. Change only one main selling angle per version. Give a headline, body, call to action, and supporting facts. Identify test metrics and claims needing review.

prompts.title: Prepare for a sales conversation
prompts.description: Bring verified context, hypotheses, and questions.
prompts.template: Prepare for a conversation with [customer role and organization] given [facts and prior contact]. List likely goals, verified information, three things to learn, and useful examples. Provide an opening and when to wrap up.

prompts.title: Practice handling a sales objection
prompts.description: Clarify the concern before answering with evidence.
prompts.template: Respond to [customer objection and available facts]. Start with a clarifying question, then give answers and evidence for likely concerns about budget, fit, or risk. Where you cannot commit, propose a check or follow-up. Give one spoken version.

prompts.title: Draft a customer proposal for review
prompts.description: Make scope, deliverables, and open terms visible.
prompts.template: Use [customer needs and confirmed terms] to draft a proposal for [customer role]. Cover goals, scope, timeline, verification, exclusions, and terms to confirm. Back up capabilities with evidence and flag missing dates or prices.

prompts.title: Write a campaign performance report
prompts.description: Explain results, attribution limits, and next actions.
prompts.template: Use [campaign goals and data] to report to [audience]. For each channel give reach, conversion, costs, and definitions. Separate observed changes from unverified attribution. Suggest one thing each to continue, stop, and measure.

prompts.title: Turn customer results into a case study
prompts.description: Structure background, obstacle, approach, and results while flagging data needing approval.
variables: customer interview notes or project facts
prompts.template: Using [customer interview notes or project facts], draft a verifiable case study for [target prospective buyers]. Cover the customer's context, the obstacle, what they implemented, verifiable results, and lessons learned. Use only facts from the material and flag any numbers that need data verification or customer approval.

prompts.title: Build a one-page competitive battlecard for sales
prompts.description: Summarize verifiable differences, where each option fits best, and answers to buyer questions.
variables: public facts or customer feedback on us and the competitor
prompts.template: Using [public facts or customer feedback on us and the competitor], create a one-page sales battlecard for [target buyer segment]. Include a one-line positioning contrast, evidence-backed strengths, scenarios where the competitor is a better fit, answers to 3 common buyer comparison questions, and claims that still need verification.

prompts.title: Plan a triggered follow-up email sequence
prompts.description: Define trigger timing, core message, single call to action, and exit rules for each email.
prompts.template: For [conversion goal and audience stage], design a [number of emails]-email follow-up sequence using [product details and available assets]. For each email, specify the trigger, wait time, core message, single call to action, exit condition, and the metric that shows whether it worked.

prompts.title: Review a pricing page from a buyer's view
prompts.description: Spot unclear tier differences, hidden costs, and terms that cause hesitation.
variables: pricing page copy or tier table
prompts.template: From the perspective of [target buyer persona], review [pricing page copy or tier table]. Check whether the differences between tiers are immediately clear, whether upgrade triggers make sense, and whether any extra fees or limits are unclear. Give 3 to 5 specific copy or structure fixes.

prompts.title: Classify and route support tickets
prompts.description: Assign work based on the issue, impact, and service scope.
prompts.template: Use [tickets and taxonomy] to label request type, main issue, affected parties, priority rationale, and queue. Allow multiple labels and ask for missing evidence. Keep ticket IDs and flag items needing human review first.

prompts.title: Write the first useful reply to a ticket
prompts.description: Confirm the goal and ask for the smallest diagnostic details.
prompts.template: Draft a first reply from [ticket and known details]. Reflect the outcome the user wants restored, state confirmed facts, and ask one or two questions that narrow the issue. Give an achievable time for the next update.

prompts.title: Write step-by-step support guidance
prompts.description: Start with low-risk, reversible checks.
variables: symptom, environment, and customer skill level
prompts.template: Write troubleshooting steps for [symptom, environment, and customer skill level]. Give the action, expected signal, and next branch if it fails. Start with reversible checks, mark support-only actions, and preserve the user's data.

prompts.title: Hand off a problem to the right team
prompts.description: Show what was tried and what the receiving team needs to do.
prompts.template: Turn [issue and troubleshooting record] into a handoff to [escalation team]. Include impact, timing, account or version scope, reproduction, attempted checks, needed decision, and next customer update. Remove unnecessary identity information.

prompts.title: Draft a service incident update
prompts.description: Share known impact, progress, and the next update time.
prompts.template: Use [verified incident details] to update [affected users]. State impact, start time, and what users can do. Give progress and the next update time. Mark cause or recovery estimates as unconfirmed if evidence is missing.

prompts.title: Write a ticket resolution note
prompts.description: Help the user verify recovery and reopen the issue if needed.
prompts.template: Turn [ticket history, fix, and verification] into a resolution note for the user. Explain what changed, how to check, any remaining impact, and how to get help again. Include a reference number safe for the user to keep.

prompts.title: Turn a resolved ticket into a knowledge base article
prompts.description: Generalize the steps and when they apply.
prompts.template: Use [verified ticket and fix] to write a knowledge base article for [readers]. Cover symptoms, scope, checks, solution, and when to escalate. Remove customer details and retain verifiable symptoms and versions.

prompts.title: Review a support reply for accuracy and follow-through
prompts.description: Check policy, evidence, tone, and next steps.
prompts.template: Use [service rules and QA criteria] to review [ticket and reply]. Check accuracy, whether the main issue is addressed, what the user must do, and whether commitments can be kept. Give a replacement line and audit note for the highest-priority issue.

prompts.title: Report on support backlogs and recurring issues
prompts.description: Separate urgent queues from measurement problems.
prompts.template: Use [queue data and time window] to report volume, duration, distributions, and recurring themes. Define waiting time, first response, and resolution. Identify queues to prioritize and anomalies that may reflect incomplete records.

prompts.title: Write a standard reply for a recurring request
prompts.description: Keep commitments consistent while allowing personalization.
prompts.template: Write a macro for [common requests and service policy]. Mark editable context fields, allowed commitments, and escalation conditions. Give an example that should use the macro and one that should not.

prompts.title: Draft a customer-facing post-incident summary (RFO)
prompts.description: Explain impact scope, verified root cause, fixes made, and concrete prevention steps.
variables: internal incident timeline and root-cause notes
prompts.template: Using [internal incident timeline and root-cause notes], draft a customer-facing post-incident summary for [affected customer group]. Cover impact window and scope, verified cause, fixes completed, and concrete steps to prevent recurrence. Avoid internal jargon and give a follow-up date for anything still under investigation.

prompts.title: Evaluate a refund or credit request against policy
prompts.description: Verify facts against policy first, then draft an internal decision note and customer reply.
prompts.template: Using [refund or credit policy], evaluate this customer request: [order facts and customer request]. First output an internal decision check (eligibility, exact policy clause, whether an exception approval is needed, and risk notes), then draft a clear, respectful customer reply with the outcome, timeline, or available alternatives.

prompts.title: Create a first-week customer onboarding guide
prompts.description: Summarize setup steps, common snags, and how to get help to prevent early tickets.
variables: setup steps and common new-user questions
prompts.template: Based on [setup steps and common new-user questions], write a first-week onboarding guide for [new customer segment]. Break it into Day 1 setup, Days 2–3 core configuration, and Days 4–7 verification, add self-checks for 3 common snags, and list what details to include if they need support.

prompts.title: Build a churn follow-up and attribution guide
prompts.description: Separate recoverable from non-recoverable churn drivers for product and support teams.
variables: customer usage notes or ticket history
prompts.template: Using [customer usage notes or ticket history] and [cancellation context], draft a low-friction follow-up guide with up to 5 questions, plus an attribution rubric separating product gaps, onboarding friction, price-to-value mismatch, and external changes so product and support teams can act on patterns.

workflows.title: From a research question to a sourced brief
workflows.description: Deliver a conclusion with enough detail for others to verify it.

workflows.title: From a meeting to decisions and follow-up
workflows.description: Prepare the agenda, then hand decisions, owners, and next steps to the team.

workflows.title: From a writing brief to publication
workflows.description: Plan, edit, and adapt a piece for a known audience.

workflows.title: Learn a new topic
workflows.description: Use explanations, exercises, and error feedback to check independent understanding.

workflows.title: Run a language practice session
workflows.description: Start at the right level, practice in context, and review your speaking.

workflows.title: Plan and check a trip
workflows.description: Verify the itinerary, packing list, and backup plans before leaving.

workflows.title: Decide what to buy
workflows.description: Narrow the options, then verify reviews, costs, and the final details.

workflows.title: From a file bundle to verifiable data
